title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADR Process
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also describes the ADR (Architectural Decision Record) workflow and includes templates and examples. The goal is to provide a single reference teams can follow to ensure interoperability, maintainability, security, and predictable production economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope

- Applies to all services owned by Platform, Serving Runtime, Eng-Infra, and public SDKs/APIs.
- Does NOT replace team-specific runbooks; it establishes company-level minimums and recommended defaults.

1) API Standards

Summary
- All public and internal REST/HTTP APIs must follow our API contract guidelines to ensure consistent developer experience and easy evolution. GraphQL is allowed for internal consumer-heavy services with approval.

Principles
- Predictability: stable URL patterns, consistent error codes, and pagination.
- Versioning: always include API version in the path (e.g. /v1/...), and avoid breaking changes within a major version.
- Backwards compatibility: additive changes only for minor versions; deprecation window of 90 days for client-visible changes.

Conventions
- Resource-based endpoints: /v1/projects/{project_id}/models/{model_id}/inference
- Use standard HTTP verbs and status codes (200, 202, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500).
- Error response schema (JSON): {
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "details": ["string"]
  }
}
- Pagination: cursor-based (next_cursor) for long lists.
- Rate limiting: 429 with Retry-After header, and structured payload to indicate remaining quota.

Authentication and AuthZ
- OAuth 2.0 (JWT bearer) for customer-facing APIs. Internal services may use mTLS or service tokens.
- RBAC enforced at gateway for platform features.

SDKs and Contract Tests
- SDKs must include contract tests that assert response shapes for all stable endpoints. Contract tests run in CI against a mocked API gateway and during canary deploys.

2) Coding Standards

General Principles
- Readability and correctness over cleverness. Prefer simple, testable implementations.
- Functions should be small and single-responsibility.

Language-specific Guidelines (high level)
- Python: follow PEP8, use type hints, and async for IO-bound handlers. Use black and mypy.
- Go: use gofmt, effective error wrapping, and context propagation for cancellation/timeout.
- Rust/CPP (low-level runtime): document unsafe blocks and isolate them behind safe interfaces; include benchmarks for kernel-critical code.

Testing and CI
- Unit tests for all new logic. Integration tests for cross-service interactions.
- Coverage target: >80% for service critical paths.
- All PRs must include changelog entry stanza and link to relevant ADRs or design docs.

Code Reviews and Merges
- Two approvers required for high-risk areas (security, infra, runtime).
- Feature flags required for user-facing changes that touch API contracts or billing flows.

3) Infrastructure Standards

Provisioning and IaC
- Terraform is the canonical IaC for cloud resources. Modules must follow the company module naming and tagging schema.
- Central state account for Terraform state with S3 + DynamoDB locking (AWS), or equivalent in other clouds.

Network and Security
- VPCs: default private subnets for compute; public subnets only for NAT and load balancers.
- Bastion and restricted SSH access; no direct DB access from developer laptops.
- Secrets: use KMS/HSM-backed secret stores (AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault for private deployments).

Capacity and Scaling
- Autoscaling targets must be based on request latency p95 and queue depth. See capacity table below.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Service Names and Ownership
- Serving runtime components: inference-gateway, model-loader, kv-cache, batch-coordinator, metrics-exporter. Each has an owner and SLO. Owners live in OWNERS files at repository root.

Model Versioning and Compatibility
- Models must be published with semantic model versions: major.minor.patch (e.g., gptx-1.4.2). Compatibility rules: major version change may imply tokenizer/IO changes and requires cross-team review.

Deployment and Rollouts
- Canary-first rollout: deploy to 1% traffic for 24 hours, escalate to 10% for 24 hours, then full. Automatic rollback on: 5xx rate > 0.5% above baseline OR latency p95 > 150% of baseline OR quality regression alerts.

KV / Prefix Caching
- Default: enable KV caching for embeddings and chat sessions; TTLs configured per-model (default 24h). Cache invalidation must be explicit for model repacks.

Quantization Profiles
- Maintain quantization profiles per model in the quantization-profiles directory. Profiles specify bitwidth (8/4), expected accuracy delta, and recommended hardware.

5) Observability Standards

Metrics and Tagging
- All services must export OpenTelemetry metrics and traces. Metric naming follows: redwood.<service>.<metric_name>. Labels/tags: service, env, region, model_version, route.

Required Metrics (minimum)
- request_count (counter)
- request_duration_seconds (histogram) with p50/p90/p95/p99 buckets
- token_count (counter)
- model_cache_hit_rate (gauge)
- model_load_time_seconds (gauge)

Tracing
- Distributed tracing must propagate correlation_id (X-Request-ID) and span IDs. Sampling: 1% by default, 20% for canary traffic, 100% on error traces.

Logging
- Structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, env, region, request_id, trace_id, message, extra. Sensitive fields must be redacted before ingest.

Alerting and Oncall
- Alert thresholds are defined in dashboards-and-alerts. Alert severity: P0 (paging), P1 (email + slack), P2 (slack only). Runbooks linked from each alert.

6) Performance Standards

SLOs and Error Budgets
- Platform API (public): 99.9% availability measured monthly; latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms for control-plane APIs, p95 < 1s for inference start (first-byte) for small-generation models (<512 tokens).
- Serving runtime: availability 99.95% for Dedicated; p99 token generation latency baseline per model documented in model catalog.

Benchmarks and Perf Tests
- All model onboarding must include standard perf-suite runs (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Benchmarks include throughput (tokens/sec), memory usage, GPU utilization, and tail latency.

Performance Optimization Checklist
1. Validate model quantization profile and accuracy delta.
2. Configure batching windows by workload type.
3. Enable prefix/KV caching where applicable.
4. Tune kernel selection via runtime flags; compare against canonical kernels.

7) Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

When to write an ADR
- Major architecture or cross-cutting design changes: introducing new runtime, changing shard or routing model, changing default quantization profile, or new infra patterns.

ADR Template (short)
- Title: short descriptive name
- Status: proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated
- Context: problem and constraints
- Decision: chosen approach and rationale
- Consequences: operational, cost, dev impact
- Alternatives considered
- Owner and reviewers

ADR Process
1. Author creates ADR draft and places it under confluence + repository adrs/ directory.
2. Notify owners and reviewers via Slack #architecture. 48-hour review window for non-urgent ADRs.
3. After review, set status to accepted and record implementation plan and migration steps.
4. Link ADR to related pages and update OWNERS if new ownership is created.

Example ADR: Unified Inference Routing (summary)
- Context: multiple routing policies across hosted/dedicated/private caused inconsistent fallbacks and difficult troubleshooting.
- Decision: adopt policy-driven smart-router that evaluates latency, cost, and model-compatibility rules. Implemented as a stateless policy engine executed at the gateway layer with feature-flagged rollout.
- Consequences: simplifies regional fallbacks, adds a single point to test routing policy, requires additional tracing for decision context.

8) Compliance and Security Considerations

- All public endpoints must pass security review prior to GA.
- Customer data in Private deployments must be encrypted at rest and in transit; provide KMS integration documentation for customers.

Tables (Quick Reference)

SLOs and thresholds
| Area | SLO | Measurement Window | Alert Threshold |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Control-plane API | 99.9% availability | monthly | <99.8% triggers P1 |
| Dedicated Serving | 99.95% availability | monthly | <99.9% triggers P0 |
| Inference latency (p95) | <1s (small gen) | 30d rolling | >1.5s triggers P1 |

Capacity planning defaults
| Component | Scale metric | Target utilization |
| inference-gateway | p95 latency & queue depth | 60-70% |
| model-loader | model-load-time | 50% |
| gpu-pool | GPU utilization | 70-80% |

9) Operational Playbook (high-level)

Rolling back a model version (owner: Serving Runtime)
1. Detect regression via quality monitors or alerts.
2. Open incident and set state to investigating.
3. Stop new traffic to suspect model (gateway rule) and shift to previous stable model version using policy engine.
4. Monitor metrics for 30 minutes; escalate if errors persist.
5. If safe, run post-rollback smoke tests and close incident.

Onboarding a new model to serving
1. Submit model onboarding PR with artifacts, quantization profile, perf results, and validation prompts.
2. QA runs verification tests and signs off.
3. Deploy to canary and run 24h canary perf & quality checks.
4. Promote to production following rollout policy.

Appendix B - ADR template (markdown)
```
# ADR <number>: <Title>
Status: proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated
Date: YYYY-MM-DD
## Context
...
## Decision
...
## Consequences
...
## Alternatives considered
...
Owner: <name>
Reviewers: <names>
```

Appendix C - Example API error JSON (copyable)
```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded for project: 12345",
    "details": ["Limit: 100 requests/min"]
  }
}
```

Notes and next steps
- This document is the canonical starting point for new standards changes. Major changes must be accompanied by ADRs and implementation plans.
- Owners: maintain the sections in each subdirectory (api-standards, infra-standards, model-serving-standards, observability-standards, performance-standards).
